starshipEstimatedLaunch.summary: SpaceX’s launch page does not list an official Flight 14 date. As of September 14, Next Spaceflight lists the first orbital Starship attempt as no earlier than September 18, 2026; its listed time is an independent estimate, not an official SpaceX schedule.

inputFacts.title: APOD: 2026 October 19 – Treble Clef: Unusual X-ray Hot Radio Source
inputFacts.summary: The Treble Clef, an unusual radio structure extending over 2 million light-years, is hypothesized to have originated from charged particles expelled by a supermassive black hole. These particles, after their radio emission faded, may have been re-energized by a shock wave resulting from the collision of two galaxy clusters.

inputFacts.title: Autumn Paints Poland’s Bieszczady Mountains
inputFacts.summary: Satellite imagery from Landsat 9 captured the seasonal transformation of Poland's Bieszczady National Park on October 8, 2026, showing fall colors in the forested slopes and tan patches of high-mountain meadows (polonina).

inputFacts.title: APOD: 2026 October 18 – Sonified: Eagle Nebula Pillars
inputFacts.summary: The Eagle Nebula (M16) contains dark, towering structures of cold gas and dust, sculpted by ultraviolet light and powerful winds from massive stars, which are likely similar to the environment where our Sun formed.

inputFacts.title: APOD: 2026 October 17 – 3D 67P
inputFacts.summary: The Rosetta spacecraft's OSIRIS camera captured images of Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko on July 25, 2015, revealing its double-lobed nucleus with dimensions of approximately 4 kilometers and 2.5 kilometers in diameter, joined by a narrow neck. Numerous jets were observed emanating from the comet's active surface.

inputFacts.title: APOD: 2026 October 16 – Chasing the International Space Station
inputFacts.summary: A Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft successfully launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, heading for low Earth orbit to rendezvous with the International Space Station on NASA's 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission.

inputFacts.title: The stakes appear high for college students who gamble
inputFacts.summary: The normalization of sports betting, particularly among young men, is a concern for college students, as many believe their sports knowledge provides an advantage or can supplement income, despite competing against a sophisticated industry designed for profit when bettors lose.

inputFacts.title: NASA Satellites Observe Historic 2026 El Niño
inputFacts.summary: NASA satellites have observed the unfolding of a historic El Niño event in 2026, characterized by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in the equatorial Pacific, rising sea surface heights, and changes in ocean color due to decreased phytoplankton abundance.

inputFacts.title: Whatcha lookin’ at? Social anxiety heightens brain sensitivity to others’ gaze
inputFacts.summary: Young adults with higher levels of social anxiety exhibit stronger brain responses when a word describing mental states conflicts with what a gaze pattern seems to convey. This heightened neural sensitivity, specifically the N400 response, suggests an increased alertness to social cues, but it does not improve their explicit judgments about the meaning of the gaze.

inputFacts.title: Many older adults make Medicare decisions quickly, most don’t change plans
inputFacts.summary: A University of Michigan survey indicates that 60% of older adults spend less than an hour choosing their Medicare coverage during Open Enrollment, with 27% not reviewing options at all and 80% retaining their previous year's coverage.

inputFacts.title: They get knocked down—but they get up again
inputFacts.summary: Low doses of the herbicide dicamba can cause the common weed oxalis (wood sorrel) to produce more flowers, a phenomenon known as hormesis. This effect is a single-generation response and does not appear to be heritable or lead to evolution in the oxalis population.

inputFacts.title: Recycle Bowl returns to Michigan Stadium after record-setting year
inputFacts.summary: The Recycle Bowl event at Michigan Stadium has successfully increased the collection of recyclable and compostable materials from game day activities each year, with over 47,000 pounds collected in 2025, demonstrating that large events can significantly boost recycling participation and material recovery.

inputFacts.title: Mollusk microbiome? It’s all in the family
inputFacts.summary: The composition of a mollusk's microbiome is primarily determined by its species (family tree) rather than its living environment. This means that mollusks of the same species will have more similar microbiomes, even if they live in different locations, than mollusks of different species living in the same environment.
